----------------

🎯 AI
===================

Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) released their AI Threat Tracker report covering adversarial AI evolution through Q2 2026. The central shift: adversaries are transitioning from basic prompting to agentic AI workflows and AI-enabled automation. Human-in-the-loop latency is dramatically reduced, compressing the traditional window for defenders to respond.

Key Operational Findings:

In Q2 2026, GTIG observed a threat actor compromise a cloud resource, then plan, build, and execute an agent-enabled mass credential harvesting campaign in under six hours. This compresses what traditionally required days of manual setup into a single afternoon. The agent autonomously managed the campaign lifecycle from planning through execution.

UNC6780 was tracked using multiple tactics to trick AI coding assistants and LLM security scanners as part of open source software supply chain compromises. This directly targets the AI-assisted development pipeline that organizations are rapidly adopting, and it challenges the assumption that AI security scanners improve defensive posture.

Q2 2026 Threat Trends:
• Expanding software supply chain risks: AI-assisted coding tools and open source integration accelerate development cycles but increase operational risk. Adversaries actively target developers, AI coding assistants, and LLM security scanning tools.
• Targeting proprietary AI IP: Increasing instances of adversaries targeting proprietary AI models, code, prompts, and research across healthcare, government, and media sectors.
• Shift toward agentic AI and automation: Multi-agent frameworks autonomously manage scanning pipelines, resolve operational errors, and execute credential harvesting at scale without human intervention.
• Multi-stage lifecycle augmentation: State-sponsored and cybercrime groups continue using AI as force multipliers across the attack lifecycle. Reconnaissance, social engineering lure creation, custom malware obfuscation, and post-exploitation troubleshooting are all augmented. Information operations campaigns are being scaled experimentally.
• Illicit account procurement and LLMJacking: Adversaries steal developer credentials, purchase compromised AI platform accounts, and hijack enterprise cloud infrastructure to run unauthorized high-performance compute workloads, circumventing access costs.

Technical Analysis:

The six-hour cloud-to-credential-harvesting timeline is the most operationally significant finding. It demonstrates that agentic AI workflows compress the attack lifecycle to a point where manual response is insufficient. Autonomous detection and response must match that speed or defenders will consistently lose the race.

The supply chain angle is equally concerning. AI coding assistants are integrated into production environments, making them high-value targets. If adversaries can trick both coding assistants and security scanners, the trust model for AI-generated and AI-verified code needs fundamental rethinking.

UNC6780's techniques against LLM security scanners are particularly notable. Defensive AI tools being fooled undermines the assumption that AI improves security posture under adversarial conditions.

The report is grounded in Mandiant frontline incident response telemetry, global threat actor tracking, and live platform defenses. Specific IoCs, CVEs, and detailed TTPs for UNC6780's supply chain techniques are not included in this excerpt.
